items.title: Cabazitaxel, Carboplatin, Cetrelimab, and Niraparib for Aggressive Variant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a combination treatment for aggressive variant metastatic prostate cancer. Patients receive chemotherapy (cabazitaxel and carboplatin) plus immunotherapy (cetrelimab), followed by a PARP inhibitor (niraparib) with or without continued immunotherapy. The study aims to determine if this combination can stop tumor growth in this hard-to-treat form of prostate cancer. The trial is no longer recruiting new patients.

items.title: AZD0516 Study for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage trial (phase 1/2) is testing AZD0516, a new investigational drug, alone and in combination with other anti-cancer agents for metastatic prostate cancer. The main goal is to assess safety and find the right dose. The study is currently recruiting patients. As an early trial of a novel agent, results may inform future treatment approaches.

items.title: Talazoparib Plus Enzalutamide Before Surgery for Prostate Cancer with Lymph Node Spread
items.summary: This phase 2 trial adds talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) to standard hormone therapy and enzalutamide before surgery in patients with prostate cancer that has spread to lymph nodes. The study tests whether adding the PARP inhibitor improves treatment effectiveness. This is for earlier-stage disease rather than advanced metastatic cancer. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Risk-Adapted Treatment with De-escalation for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial uses a personalized approach for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, matching treatment intensity to disease risk and then reducing treatment when appropriate. The goal is to maintain cancer control while reducing side effects. The study will measure progression-free survival and quality of life. Not yet recruiting patients.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Treatment for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig (a novel bispecific antibody) combined with abiraterone against standard chemotherapy or hormone therapy in chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival. This is a pivotal trial that could lead to a new treatment option. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Phase 1 Safety Study of Xaluritamig for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage trial evaluates the safety of xaluritamig, a bispecific antibody, in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine the appropriate dose and identify side effects. Currently recruiting. This supports the larger phase 3 study of the same drug.

items.title: Carboplatin Study for Metastatic Prostate Cancer with DNA Repair Defects
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial evaluated carboplatin chemotherapy specifically for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with mutations in homologous recombination repair genes. The study aimed to determine if tumors with these DNA repair defects respond better to platinum chemotherapy. Results may help identify which patients benefit from carboplatin.

items.title: Radium-223 Alone or Combined with M3814 and Avelumab for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests radium-223 (a radioactive treatment for bone metastases) alone, with M3814 (a DNA repair blocker), or with both M3814 and avelumab (immunotherapy) in castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to find the best combination to improve treatment of bone metastases. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Tinengotinib Combined with Standard Treatments for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests tinengotinib, a new drug, combined with either abiraterone or enzalutamide for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety and side effects of these combinations. Currently recruiting patients. Early-stage trial exploring a novel combination approach.

items.title: BL-B01D1 Combination Study for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2/3 trial will evaluate BL-B01D1 combination therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Limited details are available, but the study plans to start with phase 2 and potentially expand to phase 3 based on results. Not yet recruiting.

items.title: Combination Radioactive Treatment with Actinium-225 and Lutetium-177 for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests a novel combination of two radioactive treatments targeting PSMA on prostate cancer cells: actinium-225-J591 and lutetium-177-PSMA. Both deliver radiation directly to cancer cells. The study aims to find the safest dose of this dual radioactive approach. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Dual-Target CAR-NK Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates ETB-DualNK-01, a CAR-NK cell therapy targeting both PSMA and PSCA proteins on prostate cancer cells, in metastatic castration-resistant disease. The study assesses safety and early effectiveness of this novel immunotherapy approach using engineered natural killer cells. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Olaparib Combined with Radium-223 for Metastatic Prostate Cancer with Bone Spread
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial studies combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with radium-223 (radioactive treatment for bone metastases) in castration-resistant prostate cancer. The combination may enhance cancer cell death by blocking DNA repair while delivering radiation. The trial is determining the best dose. Not actively recruiting new patients.

items.title: GDC-1261 Study for Advanced or Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates GDC-1261, a new investigational drug, for advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study aims to assess safety, how the drug is processed by the body, and early signs of effectiveness. Researchers will identify recommended doses for future studies. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Multi-Target Radioligand Therapy for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial uses imaging to identify which target (PSMA, SSTR2, or GRPR) is most prominent on neuroendocrine prostate cancer cells, then delivers corresponding radioactive treatment. The study evaluates how tumor targets change after treatment and assesses safety. Not actively recruiting new patients. Addresses a rare, aggressive form of advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Pocenbrodib Alone or with Darolutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests pocenbrodib, a novel drug, alone and combined with darolutamide (a hormone therapy) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to find the right dose and assess early effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel for Metastatic Prostate Cancer with Poor Hormone Therapy Response
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy helps patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have inadequate PSA response to hormone therapy plus ARPI. The goal is to determine if early chemotherapy addition prevents progression. Currently recruiting. Addresses treatment intensification for suboptimal responders.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Versus Enzalutamide Alone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat (an investigational epigenetic drug) combined with enzalutamide against enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who haven't received prior ARPI or chemotherapy. The study tests whether adding mevrometostat improves outcomes. Currently recruiting. Pivotal trial for a novel drug combination.

items.title: FAPI PET/MRI Imaging Study for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates FAPI (fibroblast activation protein inhibitor) PET/MRI imaging for prostate cancer. The study aims to understand how FAPI binds to tumor-associated cells and whether this imaging approach can better diagnose and track prostate cancer. Participants undergo two imaging scans. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Phase 1 Study in Japanese Patients with Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety and pharmacokinetics of luxdegalutamide (JSB462), a next-generation androgen receptor inhibitor, specifically in Japanese patients with metastatic prostate cancer. Currently recruiting. Regional study to support drug development.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177-PSMA for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests luxdegalutamide (a hormone therapy) combined with lutetium-177-PSMA (radioactive treatment) compared to lutetium-177-PSMA alone in metastatic CRPC patients previously treated with at least one hormone therapy. The study will select the best dose for phase 3. Not actively recruiting new patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177-PSMA Versus Observation for Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer After Initial Treatment
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares lutetium-177-PSMA radioactive treatment to observation alone in patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer (limited spread) progressing after initial treatment. The goal is to control recurrent disease and delay need for hormone therapy while maintaining quality of life. Currently recruiting. Pivotal trial for earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: Bipolar Androgen Therapy to Restore Treatment Sensitivity in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests bipolar androgen therapy, which alternates testosterone levels between very low and very high, to restore sensitivity to hormone therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The approach may suppress cancer growth and delay progression. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Actinium-225-PSMA Plus Hormone Therapy Versus Standard Treatment for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares actinium-225-PSMA (a powerful radioactive treatment) combined with hormone therapy against standard treatment (switching hormone therapy, chemotherapy, or lutetium-177-PSMA) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is improved progression-free survival. Currently recruiting. Pivotal trial for a novel alpha-emitting radioligand.

items.title: How Inflammation Drives Treatment Resistance in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research paper reviews how chronic inflammation through NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 pathways drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. These inflammatory signals interact with androgen receptor signaling and cause epigenetic changes that promote tumor survival, spread, and resistance to therapy. Understanding these mechanisms may identify new treatment targets for advanced castration-resistant disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Response to Immunotherapy in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study demonstrates that a nanoplasmid-based DNA vaccine targeting PSMA can generate strong immune responses against prostate cancer and enhance the effectiveness of PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy. The vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastases in animal models and increased immune cell activity. This approach may help overcome resistance to immunotherapy in advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Targeting EGFR/ERK Pathway Overcomes Enzalutamide Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research identifies that prolonged enzalutamide treatment in prostate cancer with AR splice variants leads to increased EGFR expression and sustained ERK pathway activation, causing resistance. Blocking this EGFR/ERK pathway can overcome resistance in tumors expressing AR variants. The findings suggest combination therapies targeting both androgen receptor and EGFR/ERK pathways may benefit patients with treatment-resistant disease.

items.title: Real-World Results of Lutetium-177-PSMA-I&T in Brazil for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Brazilian real-world study of 43 heavily pre-treated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that lutetium-177-PSMA-I&T treatment achieved PSA reduction of 50% or more in a subset of patients. The study provides practical evidence about outcomes in patients who had received multiple prior treatments, helping inform treatment decisions for advanced disease.

items.title: Hormone Therapy Versus Chemotherapy for First-Line Metastatic Prostate Cancer Treatment
items.summary: This real-world study of 148 patients compared ARPI-based hormone therapy to docetaxel chemotherapy as first-line treatment for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. ARPI therapy showed significantly longer time before radiographic progression compared to docetaxel, while overall survival was similar. The findings provide practical evidence comparing these two standard approaches in routine clinical practice.

items.title: IL-12-Enhanced CAR-T Cell Therapy Targeting PSMA for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed an improved PSMA-targeted CAR-T cell therapy using a human-derived antibody fragment and incorporating membrane-bound IL-12 to enhance effectiveness. The IL-12 enhancement increased T cell expansion, anti-tumor activity, and IFN-γ production in laboratory models. This approach aims for safer and more effective cell therapy for advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Effects of Hormone Therapy on Radiation Dose During Lutetium-177-PSMA Treatment
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This dosimetry study examined whether continuing androgen receptor inhibitors during lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy affects radiation doses delivered to tumors. Analysis of 50 patients found no significant difference in tumor radiation doses between patients receiving concurrent hormone therapy and those who weren't. These preliminary results inform treatment planning decisions.

items.title: Hypertension Risk from Hormone Therapies in Prostate Cancer: Meta-Analysis
items.summary: This comprehensive meta-analysis of 22 studies involving over 22,000 prostate cancer patients found that androgen receptor pathway inhibitors significantly increase hypertension risk. All-grade hypertension risk increased 82%, with combination therapies showing higher risk than single agents. The findings emphasize the need for blood pressure monitoring in patients receiving these hormone therapies.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Treatment Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a novel drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT pathways to overcome c-MYC-driven resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Single-target AKT inhibitors often fail due to c-MYC upregulation, but this dual-targeting approach addresses both mechanisms. The compound showed promising anti-tumor activity in laboratory models of resistant disease.

items.title: New PSMA Imaging Agent Shows Better Pelvic Tumor Detection than Standard Scan
items.summary: This case report demonstrates that F-18-rhPSMA-7.3 PET/CT imaging detected recurrent prostate cancer in the pelvis and bladder wall that was not fully visible on standard F-18-DCFPyL PET/CT. The new agent has significantly lower urinary excretion, providing clearer images of pelvic tumors near the bladder. This may improve detection and treatment planning for pelvic disease.
